description: The configuration surface of the application-gateway chart. GENERATED from values.yaml by `./build.sh Charts` and diffed in CI — docs/plan/03 § charts/. Edit values.yaml, never this file. Members carrying `x-cybercloud-api: false` are chart or platform plumbing and are not part of the resource body.

backendPools.description: The pool members, one per entry, as pool=target:port. The target is an IPv4 address, an IPv6 address in brackets, or the resource id of a virtual machine in this network — for example web=10.20.1.11:8080 or api=/tenants/…/providers/CyberCloud.Compute/virtualMachines/api-1:8080. ⚠ A machine is resolved to its address only once this gateway has been granted read on it.

v4.description: The IPv4 address the gateway answers on, inside the subnet's range. ⚠ Required: there is no DNS inside a virtual network, so an address nobody picked is an address nothing can be pointed at.

v6.description: The IPv6 address the gateway also answers on, or empty. Lower case only.

health.description: How a pool member is decided to be up: an HTTP GET that answers 2xx or 3xx. ⚠ Probing cannot be turned off.

healthyAfter.description: How many successful probes put a member back.

intervalSeconds.description: How often each member is probed.

path.description: The path every member is probed on.

unhealthyAfter.description: How many failed probes take a member out of its pool.

limits.description: What the gateway refuses rather than passes on.

maxConnections.description: How many client connections the gateway accepts at once.

listeners.description: The HTTP listener, and the HTTPS listener when a certificate is given.

certificate.description: A vault handle — path#field, optionally @version — whose value is a PEM bundle: the certificate chain followed by its private key. Empty means no HTTPS listener. ⚠ The path must be under your own tenant's vault prefix, tenants/<tenantId>/. The value is written into a Secret the proxy mounts and never into this body.

httpPort.description: The port plain HTTP is served on.

httpsPort.description: The port HTTPS is served on. Used only when a certificate is given.

nameOverride.description: Replace the generated object-name stem. Empty means derive it from the release name.
nameOverride.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Helm plumbing. Nothing about it belongs in a resource body.

platform.description: Resource identity injected by the reconciler. Not a tenant-facing setting.

apiVersion.description: The api-version the resource was last written at, rendered into the cybercloud.io/api-version label.
apiVersion.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

managedBy.description: Value of the cybercloud.io/managed-by label. Constant, and the selector every informer filters on.
managedBy.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

namespace.description: The resource's own namespace, which is the first component of that same Subnet object's name.
namespace.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceGroup.description: Resource group name, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-group label.
resourceGroup.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceId.description: Resource GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-id label.
resourceId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

resourceType.description: Fully qualified resource type, rendered into the cybercloud.io/resource-type label.
resourceType.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

subscriptionId.description: Subscription GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/subscription-id label.
subscriptionId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

tenantId.description: Tenant GUID, rendered into the cybercloud.io/tenant-id label.
tenantId.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

virtualNetwork.description: The parent virtual network's name, which is a component of the Subnet object the gateway pod is annotated onto.
virtualNetwork.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

platform.x-cybercloud-internal-reason: Written by the reconciler from the resource's own identity. A tenant cannot set it, so it is not part of the resource body.

routingRules.description: Where each request goes, as host/path=pool — for example shop.example.com/api=api, *.example.com/=web or */=web. The host is *, a name, or *. and a suffix; the path is a prefix, matched on whole segments. ⚠ The first rule that matches wins, in the order written. A request no rule matches gets 404.

sizing.description: CPU and memory for the proxy and the firewall, each.

preset.description: How much the proxy and the firewall each get. With the firewall on, the firewall is where the CPU goes.

subnet.description: The subnet of this virtual network the gateway sits on. The frontend address below must be inside its range.

waf.description: The web application firewall: the OWASP Core Rule Set on Coraza.

crsVersion.description: The OWASP Core Rule Set version. ⚠ One is offered: the rule set is compiled into the firewall image, so a second version is a second image.

customRules.description: Rules evaluated before the rule set, in order: deny or allow, then ip <address or range>, path <prefix>, host <name>, useragent <text> or method <METHOD> — for example deny ip 203.0.113.0/24 or allow path /healthz. ⚠ allow skips the rule set for that request entirely.

exclusions.description: Rules to turn off, as a rule id (942100), a range (942100-942199), or a rule id and one request field it stops inspecting (942100:ARGS:password).

mode.description: prevention answers 403 to a request the rule set scores as an attack; detection evaluates and logs every rule and blocks nothing; off runs no firewall at all. ⚠ In prevention mode a firewall that does not answer in time is a 503, never a pass.

paranoiaLevel.description: The CRS paranoia level. 1 is the default and blocks little that is legitimate; each level above adds rules and false positives.
